stories.title: Leaseholder bills for major works to average £15k
stories.summary: Woking Borough Council reduces the combined cost to Lakeview leaseholders from £2.6m to £1.3m.

stories.title: Parks left unlocked after behaviour fears quashed
stories.summary: Runnymede Borough Council says unlocking parks overnight can save up to £45,000.

stories.title: Second church lead theft 'another blow', warden says
stories.summary: St Mary's Church, Staines had lead stolen from its roof weeks after St Peter's Church was targeted.

stories.title: Rock legends' memorabilia goes under the hammer
stories.summary: The owner says he met music icons including John Lennon, David Bowie and Jim Morrison.

stories.title: Budget Fiat 500s complete 4,000km Rome challenge
stories.summary: Stuart Bailey and a group of men took £500 Fiats from Heathrow to Rome in three days, raising £13,000.

stories.title: Scammers are exploiting AI technology, PCC warns
stories.summary: Lisa Townsend says scammers need just three seconds of a victim's voice to be able to replicate it.

stories.title: The all-female team building careers in construction
stories.summary: Women make up about 15% of the UK construction workforce, Office for National Statistics data shows.

stories.title: Asylum hotel closure date confirmed, council says
stories.summary: Stanwell Hotel has seen protests and counter-protests during its four years housing asylum seekers.

stories.title: MPs back 'urgent intervention' over hospice cuts
stories.summary: MPs from Surrey and London have called for Andy Burnham to help the Princess Alice Hospice in Esher.

stories.title: Carers charity to close after council contract withdrawn
stories.summary: Crossroads Care Surrey says it lost 90% of its income when the county council ended its contract.

stories.title: Almost 50 new homes to be built across two sites
stories.summary: The 48 new homes in Farnham will be split between the Waverley Gardens site and in Farnham Oaks.

stories.title: 'Unacceptable' postal delays continue in South East
stories.summary: MPs across Kent, Sussex and Surrey say their inboxes are full of complaints from constituents.
